newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Optus says float largely ready.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Optus says float largely ready.

text.p: Optus Communications said on Friday the plan float on the Australian Stock Exchange remained a priority and it was largely ready to go, pending the outcome of litigation between its Optus Vision and the Seven Network Ltd.
"The float remains at the top of our list, we are largely ready to go. We are awaiting the outcome of some litigation, Optus Communications chief executive Ziggy Switkowski told reporters.
The dispute centred on the relationship between Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd and Continental Cablevision of the United States, both of whom are Optus Vision shareholders.
Continental, which recently merged with U.S. West, holds 46.5 percent of Optus Vission.
The Seven Network is in dispute with other shareholders of Optus Vision over the shareholders' agreement.
The court battle is due to start on February 24.
"We remain open to discussion with Mr Stokes (Seven chairman), but the February 24 date in court looms on the horizon and we are looking forward now to our day in court," Switkowski said.
Seven Network owns about two percent of Optus Vision, a pay television group, and has an option to raise this to 15 percent.
Optus Communications, which owns 46.5 percent of Optus Vision, had been due to float in calendar 1996.
Switkowski said he was hopeful of a swift resolution of the dispute through the courts.
"We are hoping to be able to resolve that in the courts, probably expeditiously," he said.
Switkowski said the structure of the float was unlikely to have to change to reolve the impasse.
He said Optus and Mayne Nickless Ltd, which owns 25 percent of Optus Communications, remained in agreement regarding the float plans.
"We're moving forward together in our thinking about how to take the company public and we will move forward together," he said.
